data.name: Atronna
data.gender_notes: Atronna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Atronna was the goddess of fertility and the Earth. Her name means 'one who has a powerful and mighty spirit'. In Christian context, it can be interpreted as a name for a strong and nurturing woman, symbolizing the divine feminine and the power of nature. The name Atronna carries the meaning “Goddess of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Atronna usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the divine feminine and the power of nature in our lives.
data.etymology: Atronna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atronna total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: Atronna may evoke images of a strong and powerful matriarch, reminding us of historical figures such as Eve, the gardener and mother of all mankind, or the Greek goddess Demeter, who was also a goddess of agriculture, grain crops, and the harvest. The name embodies the strength, grace, and beauty that comes with the nurturing, maternal energy of the feminine.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeply spiritual level, Atronna's name can evoke feelings of connectivity and harmony with the natural world. As a Christian interpretation of the name, it may inspire a sense of awe and reverence for the power of creation, and a reminder of God's endless love and nurturing care for all living beings. Additionally, the name may be seen as a reminder of the divinity that lies within each of us, and the power we hold to cultivate growth and nurture the embryonic potential within ourselves and in the world around us.
